input.quote: a. Grant. TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface in the ordinary course of its business of the origination, underwriting, processing and funding of consumer finance receivables in accordance with this Agreement.
input.rationale: The grant in Section 2(a) runs to Client alone; neither affiliates nor contractors acting on Client's behalf are licensed, and the scope provisions (2(b)) only add multi-site access, giving no path to extend use to group companies or outsourced providers. That fails even the fallback (affiliates covered on written notice). The licence is not expressly revocable at will — it runs until termination of the Agreement (2(c)) — so that limb is acceptable, but the assignment clause (Section 15) permits transfer only to an affiliate, not to a successor in an M&A transaction, which is also part of the fallback. Redline adds affiliates and contractors to the grant and successor transfer to Section 15; the shortcomings on perpetuity/irrevocability of paid-up licences are noted but not pressed given the subscription-style hosting bargain.

proposal.summary: Extend licence grant to Client's affiliates and contractors and permit transfer to a successor
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have extended the licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, since our group and outsourced providers will need to use the Interface in the ordinary course, and confirmed the licence transfers to a successor in an M&A transaction. If helpful, we can instead cover affiliates on written notice to TrueLink.

ops.oldText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client a non-exclusive license to use the Interface
ops.newText: TrueLink hereby grants to Client, its affiliates and its contractors acting on Client's behalf a non-exclusive license to use the Interface

ops.oldText: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or to a successor in interest by merger, acquisition or sale of all or substantially all of the assigning party's assets.
